newsitem.title: UK: Wall St aids Euro-markets, Russia nervous.
newsitem.headline: Wall St aids Euro-markets, Russia nervous.

text.p: Wall Street's return to the record books overnight breathed new life into Europe's bourses on Thursday, but a power struggle in Moscow jolted Russian markets.
Russian shares and bonds fell in jumpy trading after Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov accused security chief Alexander Lebed of plotting a "creeping coup".
"There was panic in the morning," said a trader at the Troika-Dialog bank in Moscow. "The market is very sensitive to political news and it causes panicky movements from both brokers and investors."

Elsewhere in the markets, the dollar probed higher during the morning but crude oil prices eased back further from this week's six-year highs of more than $25 a barrel. Benchmark Brent December was quoted at $23.80 by late morning, down 14 cents. The overnight performance of U.S. blue-chip stocks, which set record highs for the second time in three days, provided the early impetus in Europe.
London made a firm start, reviving after its record-breaking run faltered on Wednesday, but French and German shares ended the morning hovering around their opening levels.
Traders said they were focusing on on U.S. industrial production and capacity utilisation numbers for September, due at 1315 GMT.
The Wall Street bounce reassured British investors, boosting the blue chip FTSE 100 index by 12 points at 4,036 by the end of the morning session.
Drugs company Zeneca reached a new peak as press reports renewed talk of a bid from Switzerland's Roche and electronics retailer Dixons rose on positive comments from UBS and HSBC James Capel.
Traders said volumes remained thin, however, and investors may prove reluctant in the short term to chase the market through its recent record highs.
"Basically, we have just acknowledged the turnaround on Wall Street but I don't get the feeling there is much enthusiasm out there," said one.
French shares turned higher after a weak start, following financial futures.
The CAC-40 index was also pushed up by a 26 percent rise in Lagardere Groupe following the government's stated preference for its bid to buy Thomson SA.
But like London, dealers said bourse trading was limited and investors cautious ahead of the U.S. data due later.
German shares were stable around opening levels as traders picked selected stocks to move higher. Daimler, Siemens, SAP and banking stocks traded higher, but chemical companies saw profit-taking.
The dollar's retreat below 1.54 marks weighed on German market sentiment, although the U.S. currency edged higher in European trade during the morning.
The dollar tested 1.54 marks as the German currency fell from its highs against the Italian lira and Spanish peseta.
In contrast, the high-flying British pound strengthened across the board, shrugging off overnight profit-taking to hover near 2.4440 marks.
CURRENCIES AT 1100 GMT
The dollar was trading at 1.5393 marks and 112.16 yen, compared with 1.5383 and 112.22 in late European business on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1100 GMT
London - The FTSE index was up 12.2 points at 4,036.6.
Frankfurt - The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was trading down 0.29 points at 2,714.61.
Paris - The CAC-40 share index was up 1.22 points at 2,159.74.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed lower at $380.55 an ounce, compared with $381.50 on Wednesday afternoon and a London close of $381.75. Silver was eight cents weaker at $4.98.
